key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over 24-48 hours, often following skin break (cut, scrape, insect bite). LOCATION: Lower extremities most common, but can occur anywhere. DURATION: Progressive over 24-48 hours, may worsen rapidly. CHARACTER: ERYTHEMATOUS (red), WARM, TENDER, EDEMATOUS (swollen) skin. AGGRAVATING: TOUCH, pressure, movement. RELIEVING: ELEVATION, cool compresses, antibiotics. TIMING: Progressive over 24-48 hours, may spread rapidly. SEVERITY: 5-9/10 pain, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: FEVER (100-102°F), chills, malaise, lymphangitis (red streaks), lymphadenopathy (swollen lymph nodes), may have purulent drainage. KEY POSITIVES: Erythema, warmth, tenderness, edema, fever, lymphangitis. KEY NEGATIVES: No crepitus (rules out necrotizing fasciitis), no bullae or skin necrosis, no systemic shock.

red_flags: High fever >102°F with rigors - possible sepsis, call 911
Rapidly spreading redness with severe pain - possible necrotizing fasciitis, call 911
Bullae, skin necrosis, or crepitus - necrotizing fasciitis, call 911
Severe systemic symptoms - hypotension, tachycardia, altered mental status - sepsis, call 911
Red streaks extending from infection site - lymphangitis, needs urgent evaluation
